description: Roman sculptors often adapted the forms of earlier Greek artworks for use in entirely new contexts. This statue evokes the figures of seated, draped goddesses displayed at the Parthenon, the renowned temple on the Acropolis in Athens. Among the Romans, this statue type was used for sculptures of female deities such as Juno (Hera to the Greeks), the consort of Jupiter (Zeus to the Greeks), as well as for portraits of empresses and other women.
title: Statue of a Seated Woman
